summary: A survey of how the sons and daughters of Castro, Saddam Hussein, Stalin, Ceaușescu, Mussolini, Gaddafi and Lukashenko fared, from Uday Hussein's torture and killings to Svetlana Stalin's defection, plus a Frenchman who believed he was Hitler's son.

evidence.note: Castro segment opens: Fidelito's kidnapping, the nuclear reactor, Antonio catfished
Uday runs Iraq's national football team and beats players; later Saadi Gaddafi's football career
Stalin's children: Svetlana, Vasily and Yakov from the 1920s through WWII and her later defection
Ceausescu children in Romania; Nicu's role in the 1989 revolution massacre and later prison term
Mussolini's children: Vittorio in Hollywood, Edda's admiration for Hitler, granddaughter in politics
Long Gaddafi segment covering Saadi, Mutassim, Hannibal and Saif al-Islam up to 2017
Lukashenko's young son groomed as heir, described as he was at release in 2018
Jean-Marie Loret, born after a 1917 WWI affair in occupied France, believed Hitler was his father

notes: Survey episode with no single bastard; primary is the group of dictators' children. Origin is capped at four codes, so RO, IT, BY and FR are left out of origin despite real segments; IT and BY also miss setting (cap of six). Roles are a loose fit for a mixed group. Svetlana's later life and Loret's story push covered_span wide.
